description: v2.1.0 sections 6 and 22 — a base criminal offense expressed as typed fixed slots rather than a monolithic article unit.

statutory_refs.description: e.g. ['형법 제347조 제1항']. Open Question #13 (v2.1.0 section 25) — final article-to-doctrine mapping is a separate legal-review step; this field only records the reference, it does not carry legal effect.

elements.description: All seven fixed slots (section 6) are optional here — not every offense uses every slot (e.g. a conduct-only offense may omit causation/result). Absence means the slot is not part of this offense's constitutive elements, not that it is trivially satisfied.

element_modules.description: ElementBundleDef ids used inside this offense's elements (section 7). Listed here for discoverability/dependency tracking even though the actual reference lives inside the element_expression tree via op:ref.

exports.description: Named export map for PROJECT (section 9.3), e.g. { "result": "injury_result" }. Keys are free-form export names, not restricted to fixed_slot_name, matching ExportedComponentDef.export_key.

qualifiers.description: QualifierDef ids that may legitimately QUALIFY this offense (e.g. embezzlement listing occupational_status). This is a menu of applicable qualifiers declared at the base offense, not an application — QUALIFY itself happens in DerivedOffenseDef.

composition_metadata.description: Reserved for compiler bookkeeping. Deliberately untyped/open at this stage — v2.1.0 section 22 lists the field name but does not specify contents, and no compiler exists yet to define what it needs (step 4, QUALIFY/COMPOSE compiler, comes later in the section-26 implementation order).
